newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Senate wants HK joint declaration respected.
newsitem.headline: Italy Senate wants HK joint declaration respected.

text.p: The Italian Senate (upper house) on Wednesday urged the government to call for Hong Kong's democratically-elected assembly to be protected when the British colony is handed over to Chinese rule in three months time.

The Senate, voting on a motion presented by leftist senator Tana de Zulueta, called for the centre-left government to convey to all sides its support for "full implementation of the joint declaration regarding the electoral mandate conferred on the elected assembly in accordance with the declaration".

Under the 1984 Sino-British joint declaration, which fixed the handover for midnight on June 30, 1997, China pledged to grant Hong Kong a "high degree of autonomy" and to allow it to retain its capitalist system for 50 years.
China has already picked a Chief Executive-designate and 60-member provisional post-colonial legislature, which includes 10 politicians defeated in legislative elections in 1995.
De Zulueta said in a statement it would be very serious for Hong Kong's six million citizens to lose their political rights.
The United States has already made clear it expects China to stand by the joint declaration after the handover and de Zulueta said the Senate motion echoed similar U.S. parliamentary moves.
